'''Margaret A. Phillips''' (born November 3, 1959) is an American biologist who is the Sam G. Winstead and F. Andrew Bell Distinguished Chair in Biochemistry at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]]. She was elected a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=2021 NAS Election|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426172730/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 26, 2021|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Phillips was born in [[Cleveland]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Margaret Phillips, Ph.D. - Faculty Profile - UT Southwestern|url=https://profiles.utsouthwestern.edu/profile/15701/margaret-phillips.html|access-date=2021-05-10|website=profiles.utsouthwestern.edu|language=en-US}}</ref> She was an undergraduate student at the [[University of California, Davis]], where she studied biochemistry.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Meet the PI: Phillips Lab – UT Southwestern, Dallas, Texas|url=https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/labs/phillips/about/meet-the-pi.html|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.utsouthwestern.edu}}</ref> In 1981, Philips joined Syva, a biochemistry company in [[Palo Alto, California]].<ref name=":1" /> After two years she returned to university, as a graduate student at the [[University of California, San Francisco]] and the laboratory of [[C. C. Wang]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-08-28|title=Remembering C.C. Wang|url=https://pharmacy.ucsf.edu/news/2017/08/remembering-cc-wang|access-date=2021-05-10|website=UCSF School of Pharmacy|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Giving parasites their due|url=https://www.asbmb.org/asbmb-today/people/030116/giving-parasites-their-due|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.asbmb.org|language=en}}</ref> She remained at the University of California, San Francisco as a postdoctoral scholar with [[William J. Rutter]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Two UTSW Faculty Elected to Prestigious National Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.newswise.com/articles/two-utsw-faculty-elected-to-prestigious-national-academy-of-sciences|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.newswise.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Phillips was appointed to the faculty at the [[University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center]] in 1992, where she was promoted to Carolyn R. Bacon Professor in 2009 and Chair of the Department in 2016.<ref name=":2" /> Her research considers the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of malaria.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Researchers have shown that a drug currently in testing shows potential to cure malaria|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2015-07/usmc-rhs071515.php|access-date=2021-05-10|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 1999 Scholar Award in Molecular Parasitology<ref name=":1" />
* 2010 Medicines for Malaria Venture Project of the Year<ref>{{Cite web|title=UT Southwestern research team's anti-malarial work wins international Project of the Year award|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2011-06/usmc-usr060611.php|access-date=2021-05-10|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref>
* 2021 Elected Fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" />
